page: Microsoft Azure D32plds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the ARM architecture. It is powered by Microsoft's custom ARM Neoverse-N2 implementation running at 3.4 GHz under Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs with a 1:1 thread-to-core mapping. It is configured with 64.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core), 128 MB of shared L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 64 KB of L1 data cache per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 1888 GB NVMe SSD, and it carries no integrated GPUs.

Benchmark results highlight strong multi-threaded execution and exceptional memory throughput. In stress-ng, the multi-core score reaches 66,296.43, placing it in the top 25%, while single-core performance remains average at 2,073.49. Geekbench metrics reinforce this trend with a multi-core score of 19,774.0 and software compilation throughput of 39,729.0. Memory bandwidth delivers top-tier performance, registering 450.77 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 169.21 GB/sec for uncached writes, driving a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3,286.13.

Data-oriented workload benchmarks demonstrate high processing efficiency. PassMark database operations hit 37,222.49 in the top 10%, supported by strong Redis SET throughput of 61.98 million operations per second and static web serving speeds of 53.68 GB/sec. Conversely, CPU-only large language model inference shows clear limits, dropping to 4.66 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 70B model due to the absence of dedicated matrix accelerators and GPU hardware.

With a lower memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core paired with high-speed local NVMe storage and high multi-core scaling, the instance provides strong resource efficiency for compute-dense workloads. It is well matched for software compilation, distributed web services, caching tiers, and localized database workloads, while workloads requiring massive memory per thread or GPU acceleration will face constraints.
